front noun

the forepart

also the front, at the front, façade, front side, front of the house

classical

Caes. BC 3.37.1: ante frontem castrōrum (Lewis & Short)
Ov. F. 1.135
Traupman 319

frōns, frontis f.

noun, third declension · Declension on Wiktionary

the front; the face of a building, a camp or a line

Properly the forehead, then the front of anything, as against its back (tergum) and its sides. In front is ā fronte (Cic. Phil. 3.32, Lewis & Short; Traupman 319).

Other words

  • pars prior — the front part

    also used · classical · Plin. NH 11.131: ā priōre parte capitis (Lewis & Short); Traupman 29, 319

    Traupman’s phrase for the front of a classroom: prior pars conclāvis scholāris (p. 319).

  • prīmōris, prīmōre — front (of teeth, feet)

    also used · classical · Traupman 319 · Declension on Wiktionary

Examples

  • omnis habet geminās, hinc atque hinc, jānua frontīs, ē quibus haec populum spectat, at illa Larem

    every door has two fronts, this side and that: one looks out on the people, the other on the household godOv. F. 1.135–136

  • ā fronte

    in frontTraupman 319

  • prior pars conclāvis scholāris

    the front of the classroomTraupman 319

  • frōns aedium

    the front of the houseTraupman 319

See also in front of, front door, front seat, back to front, behind.
